expected.summary: Confirmed with its token (two-step), after pcb update: the preview lists the outline changes; the board is saved, reopened, and the outline read back from the file.
Confirmed, with nothing changed since the last save: the preview lists no change; the board is saved and reported clean.
The session has no such document open.
A Designer and a Layout are both running (the usual state once the board exists), and the call names neither --session nor --doc: E_AMBIGUOUS lists both instances with their documents.

A forward-annotation job on this board has ended, and no job get or job list has read its end yet, so its operation still locks part of the board, and the save of the whole file waits for it: E_CONFLICT target_locked.
Run under a scope file that does not cover the target (the board file); nothing is previewed to the application's files or sent.

While a forward-annotation run or pcb export job of this tool runs in Layout, the session reports busy or unresponsive. Only --session is given: Layout does not say which board it has open while it does not answer, and a --doc it cannot match would be E_NOT_FOUND.

A person leaves a modal dialog open in Layout before the call, such as Setup > Setup Parameters or Help > About. Layout stops answering COM, the session is reported blocked with the dialog's title; E_HUMAN_REQUIRED with action dismiss_dialog and a resume command. Only --session is given, since a blocked Layout does not say which board it has open.
Layout goes away after Save was sent; the board stays locked until operation resolve.

rows.unrunnable: The COM connection to Layout cannot be cut on demand at the moment of a call; driver tests D06 and D21 cover how the runtime handles a lost connection.

expected.summary: Confirmed, after a person edited the board in Layout and the tool did not: the adapter does not see a person's edits (knowledge xpedition-external-edits-not-tracked), so the preview lists no change, and the save writes the person's edits too.

Confirmed, after pcb update made the outline 70 x 48 mm and a person then dragged an outline edge in Layout: the preview lists the tool's width, the saved file holds the person's, so width_mm read back from the reopened board differs.
